before: If your childhood meant avoiding pain and keeping the people you needed close, your attention got used up reading danger (was that sigh about me?) and meeting their expectations, and when curiosity or mistakes got you punished, or it felt like they loved you less, you got better at the part. That left much less room for experiments that show you what you like when nobody's grading you. People grow into who they are by trying things on and then changing their minds, from what they wear down to the ideas and roles they take up, like a teenager who starts spelling her name with an "i" at the end and later changes it back.

guide_passage:
The r4 guide's passage (the passage this carries):
Recovery includes more than uncovering a fully formed “true self” hidden underneath. Some of it is developmental pl/ork you get to do late: creating enough safety for preference, curiosity, and experimentation to finally grow.

Reparenting and identity-building can usually proceed together. But when a firmly held identity includes a current intention to exploit or harm vulnerability, identity and adult-agency work come first; do not bring the child forward to help dismantle the identity. For some people the child-self is already easy to feel. For others, creating the conditions for it to emerge is the first phase.
